newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-UMPIRES RENEW WALKOUT THREAT, FEDERAL COURT HEARING SET.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-UMPIRES RENEW WALKOUT THREAT, FEDERAL COURT HEARING SET.

text.p: Baseball umpires revived their playoff-season boycott threat Thursday, setting the stage for a federal court hearing Friday on a request by Major League Baseball to block the walkout.
The hearing will begin at 10:00 a.m. EDT in the courtroom of U.S. District Judge Edmund Ludwig, a court official said.

The umpires' threat to boycott post-season games was renewed after Baltimore Orioles' second baseman Roberto Alomar withdrew his appeal of a five-day suspension Wednesday and the American League said the suspension would begin next season.

The umpires, who seek immediate implementation of Alomar's suspension, had agreed Tuesday to continue working provided his appeal hearing was held Thursday and a decision rendered. As part of the agreement, the two sides said they would go back in court Friday if either side charged a breach of faith.

Alomar, who spit in the face of an umpire in a game last Friday, has continued playing for the Orioles, who won the first two games of a playoff against the Indians in Baltimore. Their best-of-five series shifts to Cleveland Friday.
Earlier on Thursday, Richie Phillips, chief counsel for the umpires, said the umpires were not satisfied with Alomar's punishment.

"We're asking that he (Alomar) be suspended immediately," Phillips told ESPN Radio. "We feel that (American League president) Gene Budig has the right to modify the penalty and put it into effect at this time."
The umpires' contract contains a no-strike provision, but they have threatened not to work because of the handling of the spitting incident.

National League umpire Bruce Froemming told the radio network: "We are on a collision course like you would not believe today. Richie Phillips will see this to the wall. We have to counter Gene Budig's weakness."
Froemming ripped Budig for a lack of leadership and said the personal safety of umpires was a larger issue in the case.
"What's to stop a guy from punching one of us?" Froemming said. "He (Budig) has duties to protect his people that work for him and it's a sad state of leadership."
Umpire John Hirschbeck ejected Alomar for arguing a called third strike in a game in Toronto against the Blue Jays. An enraged Alomar spit in Hirschbeck's face after being ejected.

Days after saying he had no regrets over the incident, Alomar issued an apology to Hirschbeck and his family and donated $50,000 for research into the rare disease that took the life of one Hirschbeck's sons and afflicts another.
Alomar had exacerbated the situation by saying Hirschbeck had become a bitter man after the death of his young son.
